tools.change: SECOND PASS (verdict unchanged: revise). SAFETY, AND LIVE IN UZBEKISTAN (both kidney tools are switched on here; they are off in several other packs). Carried from the United States second pass, which read the KDIGO 2024 texts: (a) the tool shows a risk colour when no urine result was typed: an eGFR of 75 and nothing else reads "Past xavf (yashil katak)", though the risk cell is defined by two results; (b) it calls three things a "KDIGO boʻyicha nefrologga yoʻllash mezoni" that are not on the list read: any ratio above 300 mg/g (the list read asks for it together with haematuria, or a much higher ratio), a fall of more than 25% in a year (the list read speaks of a sustained fall of more than 20%), and "the very-high-risk cell" (not on the list). Example: eGFR 75, ratio 350 mg/g, no blood in the urine: the screen says a KDIGO referral criterion is met; by the list read it is not. FOUND RIGHT: the albumin categories at 30 and 300 mg/g and the GFR categories. UZBEKISTAN: the national protocol for chronic kidney disease never surfaced (six searches), so the unit laboratories print for the ratio is STILL unverified and no national referral list could be compared. A national protocol read in this pass (order No. 180 of 23.06.2025, annex 3) lists CKD-EPI and MDRD among its abbreviations and uses the Cockcroft-Gault formula for creatinine clearance when an anticoagulant is needed. Remove the word KDIGO from the referral flags or rewrite them to the list; show no colour without a urine result. — FIRST PASS: (1) The pack states the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio in mg/g and marks that as unverified: confirm the unit local laboratories print before a doctor relies on it. (2) The doctor must type an eGFR; the build has no calculator from creatinine. Add one (Part 2), with creatinine in the unit local laboratories print. (3) The referral flags and the flag "fell by more than a quarter against a year ago" are guidance, not arithmetic: confirm them against the national protocol for chronic kidney disease, which was not found. (4) It answers a question every doctor of adults asks; in the core set it is shown to every doctor role, not to internal medicine alone. The grid itself was read against the kit's own citation only; the KDIGO text was not fetched.

addTools.proposedName: Body mass index and waist circumference
addTools.nationalSourceNote: The 2015 national cardiology protocols (Ministry of Health, project "Zdorovye-3") use body mass index and waist circumference in the stable-angina and heart-failure protocols.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: Arithmetic on weight and height. The classification bands are the World Health Organization's; the publication was not fetched in this session, and neither the formula nor a band is written here.
addTools.licence: the arithmetic is free; WHO's wording needs permission for commercial use (WHO's copyright page)
addTools.secondPassNote: NATIONAL SOURCE: the national antenatal-care protocols (2021) tell the clinician to work out the body mass index and print its classes; the 2015 cardiology collection uses the index and waist circumference. PRIMARY: WHO's own page states the calculation and the adult classes and cites WHO Technical Report Series No. 854 (1995); it does not mention waist circumference, whose limits therefore rest on the national text alone. No class limit is written here.

addTools.proposedName: Kidney function: eGFR from creatinine in the laboratory's own unit, feeding the KDIGO category tool
addTools.nationalSourceNote: The national protocol for chronic kidney disease was not found, so which equation it prescribes is unverified.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:1737-1749 (the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation), as referenced on a secondary page read today; the article itself was not opened.
addTools.licence: the equation is a published fact; the article is "Copyright © 2021 Massachusetts Medical Society", for personal use only: its text and tables may not be copied
addTools.secondPassNote: NATIONAL SOURCE, partial: a national protocol (order No. 180 of 23.06.2025, annex 3) lists CKD-EPI and MDRD among its abbreviations and prescribes the Cockcroft-Gault formula for creatinine clearance; the national protocol for chronic kidney disease never surfaced, so WHICH equation it prescribes is unverified and a local nephrologist names it before anything is built. PRIMARY: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:1737-49 was opened (a repository copy): the equation without race takes age, sex and serum creatinine, the paper writes creatinine in mg/dL and gives the same conversion to micromoles per litre as the kit holds. The equation is not written here.

addTools.proposedName: Infectious-disease notification (today the slot enfeksiyon-bildirim of one specialty)
addTools.nationalSourceNote: The body is the Committee for Sanitary-Epidemiological Welfare and Public Health under the Ministry of Health (Presidential resolution PP-4790 of 27.07.2020). Its list of notifiable diseases and the report form were not read.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: No formula: a form and a list of an authority.
addTools.secondPassNote: DROPPED AS A PROPOSAL (the slot enfeksiyon-bildirim stays, unverified, for one specialty). No national source for the list of notifiable diseases, the form or the time limit was found in five searches; the law on sanitary-epidemiological well-being, read, holds none of the three as returned. It comes back as a core tool when a local epidemiologist or a lawyer names the act.

addTools.proposedName: Ten-year cardiovascular risk for the very-high-risk region (today the slot kv-risk-score2)
addTools.nationalSourceNote: WHO Europe: WHO PEN protocols 1, 2 and 3 were adapted for primary care in Uzbekistan (workshop report, 2017), and the pilot assessed total cardiovascular risk in adults of 40 and over (good-practice brief, 2018: https://who-sandbox.squiz.cloud/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/367288/gpb-hss-ncds-uzb-eng.pdf). Which chart the current national protocol prescribes is unverified.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: SCORE2 working group and ESC Cardiovascular risk collaboration. Eur Heart J 2021;42:2439-2454, with its supplementary tables for the coefficients; SCORE2-OP: Eur Heart J 2021;42:2455-2467. WHO charts: Lancet Glob Health 2019;7:e1332-e1345 (https://dspace.library.uu.nl/handle/1874/390215).
addTools.licence: needs permission for either chart: the European society authorises no commercial use of its guidelines; WHO's module is non-commercial and WHO requires permission for commercial uses
addTools.secondPassNote: NATIONAL SOURCE: the national clinical standard for arterial hypertension (annex 2 to order No. 290 of 09.09.2024) names the "Шкала SCORE" at each visit to the general practitioner; the 2015 collection orders a yearly assessment by the WHO/ISH table. Neither names SCORE2 or a region, so a local cardiologist says which chart is meant. PRIMARY: the SCORE2 paper (first pass: Uzbekistan in the very-high-risk region) and WHO's HEARTS module of 2020 (opened: Uzbekistan in the "Central Asia" chart region, cholesterol in mmol/L, a laboratory and a non-laboratory chart). It stays a slot, off.

addTools.proposedName: NYHA functional class as a record
addTools.nationalSourceNote: The 2015 national heart-failure protocol classifies by NYHA ("Классификация ХСН по NYHA").
addTools.formulaSourceNote: The classification of the New York Heart Association; its primary publication was not fetched. The kit's switched-off follow-up mechanism (kardiyo-izlem) already has the field, with classes I to IV.
addTools.secondPassNote: DROPPED AS A SEPARATE PROPOSAL. The national source stands (the 2015 heart-failure protocol classifies by NYHA; read again), but the publication that defines the classes was not reached, and the rule of this pass is both or neither. Nothing is lost: the kit's switched-off follow-up mechanism kardiyo-izlem already records the class as the doctor chooses it, and that slot now has national sources.

addTools.proposedName: Gestational age and expected date of birth (the arithmetic only, split from the antenatal schedule)
addTools.nationalSourceNote: The national antenatal protocol was not found; the dating rule must be taken from it.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: Date arithmetic; the rule to count from is the protocol's.
addTools.secondPassNote: NATIONAL SOURCE AND RULE: the national antenatal-care protocols (Ministry of Health and the Republican Specialised Scientific-Practical Medical Centre of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 2021) state the dating rule (from the last menstrual period, with the ultrasound date replacing it under a stated condition, and a rule after assisted reproduction). The rule is taken from that text by a local obstetrician; it is not written here. Whether a newer edition is in force was not found.

addTools.proposedName: Vaccination status against the national calendar (today the slots asi-takvimi and aile-asi-tarama)
addTools.formulaSourceNote: No formula: a calendar of an authority, entered and signed by a local clinician.
addTools.secondPassNote: NATIONAL SOURCE: SanQvaM 0239-07/3 (read again; amendment of 19.07.2021 the latest shown), under article 33 of the law on sanitary-epidemiological well-being (No. ZRU-393 of 26.08.2015), by which the Chief State Sanitary Doctor approves the national calendar. No formula. It stays a slot until a local clinician enters and signs the calendar.

addTools.proposedName: Growth for age against the standard the national programme names (today the slot buyume-persentil)
addTools.nationalSourceNote: No order naming the standard was found. A 2025 local paper uses WHO standards (https://inscience.uz/index.php/preventive-medicine/article/download/7502/7294/23221).
addTools.formulaSourceNote: WHO Child Growth Standards (2006), as cited by that paper; the WHO tables were not fetched.
addTools.licence: needs permission for commercial use — WHO material
addTools.secondPassNote: DROPPED AS A PROPOSAL (the slot buyume-persentil stays, unverified). No order or programme naming a growth standard was found in five searches of this pass, nor in the first pass. WHO requires permission for commercial uses of its material.

addTools.proposedName: Degree of hearing loss in the local classification (a revision of odyometri-pta)
addTools.formulaSourceNote: To be named by a local surdolog.
addTools.secondPassNote: DROPPED AS A SEPARATE PROPOSAL and folded into the verdict on odyometri-pta (revise). No national classification was found; one paper of a national specialised centre writes the first degree as 20 to 40 dB, which is not the tool's limit.

addTools.proposedName: Candidates no source was read for, each to be confirmed by a local specialist before anything is built: Glasgow Coma Scale record (emergency care, neurology, neurosurgery, anaesthesiology); Apgar record (paediatrics, obstetrics); a stroke-risk and a bleeding score for atrial fibrillation (cardiology, internal medicine); a liver-function class (gastroenterology, infectious diseases); a breathlessness grade (pulmonology); body surface area (oncology); a tooth chart (stomatology, if added)
addTools.nationalSourceNote: unverified — needs a local clinician. No national protocol naming any of these was read.
addTools.formulaSourceNote: Not fetched. No formula, item or cut-off is written here.
addTools.secondPassNote: DROPPED: seven candidates named from general knowledge, none confirmed by a national source and a primary publication together. Two have a lead for a later pass, not a proposal: a stroke-risk score for atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc stands in the abbreviation list of the 2025 national protocol on chronic ischaemic heart disease, which does not apply it) and creatinine clearance by Cockcroft-Gault (the same protocol prescribes it; its 1976 publication was not opened by any pass).
